newsitem.title: USA: INSTANT VIEW -- U.S. Aug CPI rose 0.1 pct.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW -- U.S. Aug CPI rose 0.1 pct.

text.p: Following are comments from U.S. economists after the Labor Department reported the August Consumer Price Index (CPI) rose 0.1 percent, while the core index rose 0.1 percent.
Economists in a Reuters poll had expected a 0.2-percent rise in both the overall and core rates.
DAVID BLITZER, CHIEF ECONOMIST, STANDARD AND POOR'S CORP:
"I don't think it is enough to prevent a Fed rate hike, but that's the hope that is clearly in the market right now."
Blitzer was commenting on CPI and August retail sales.
Speaking on Reuters Financial Television, Blitzer said he still expected the U.S. central bank to raise short-term interest rates by 25 basis points.

KEVIN FLANAGAN, VICE PRESIDENT AND ECONOMIST, DEAN WITTER REYNOLDS INC: "CPI shows you at the retail level, because these measure retail prices, you are not seeing any meaningful upward pressures, higher prices or any increase in prices remain on the subdued side. Pretty much anyway you slice it, (CPI) is a positive figure; it's something that will probably be welcomed by the Federal Reserve as well."

PATRICK DIMICK, ECONOMIST, CS FIRST BOSTON CORP: "This is very important because it's taking the Fed out of action for the September meeting. It allows the Fed to be staring at a low unemployment rate and say it's ok because it's not going any lower. It provides them with an excuse to endure a low unemployment rate that's scaring people. That's worth 20 basis points to the (Treasury) market. We're looking at the two year, and there's still some more juice to this rally.
"Polling through the details of CPI, we noticed apparel continues to be extremely soft. It's been flat to negative for the past eight months.

Dimick continued: "The housing sector and housing services, which was the problem in last month's report, returned to trend-like readings. There's nothing in here that would cause you to dismiss low readings of CPI.

"The (Treasury) market has priced a below 50 percent (chance that the Fed will raise rates). It's never completely out of the market. Fed funds are now trading 10 basis points above target, so now there's a 40-percent chance the Fed will go." -- N.A. Treasury Desk, 212-858-1660
